title: After That Reach
description:
Months have passed since he texted first. "Hey, let's grab a meal."

The question now is what that message turned into. Whether the first awkward reach was the start of something — or just an obligation both sides checked off.

choices.text: They started meeting more often after that
choices.result_text:
Reaching out first seemed small. Turned out to be the turning point.

The other person had been waiting for someone to go first too. The group chat started buzzing again.

That one awkward message was the thing that needed to happen. He just had to be the one who went first.

"Let's do this again soon." That's what they said when they parted.

The "soon" still hasn't come.

But reaching out in the first place was the right call, regardless of what came after.

title: His World, Revisited
description:
At the wedding reception, seeing a table of strangers — he accepted that his friend had built a whole world without him. And meant it.

Something about that shifted things. They've felt closer since, in a way that's hard to explain.

Today his friend reached out.

choices.text: They met up. Even talked about the strangers at the wedding.
choices.result_text:
"You had so many people at your wedding."
"Yeah. How have you been?"

That question came easier than before.

The moment he genuinely accepted his friend's world expanding — he became part of it.

choices.text: Just texted back. Haven't met yet.
choices.result_text:
"We should catch up properly." That text is still sitting there.

No date set yet. But they're in contact — and that's already different from before.

Some relationships are fine at a slow pace.

title: The Series A, Revisited
description:
The university friend who closed a 5 billion won Series A.
The one he genuinely congratulated.

Curious how things went, he looked it up.
Something came up in the news.

choices.text: Doing well — closed a Series B
choices.result_text:
Series B. 12 billion won.

Another article. Complicated feelings? Sure — he'd be lying if he said no.
But something else was there too this time.

Not 'someday me too' — more like 'in my own way too.'
His friend's success now shows him his own direction, not just the gap.

Not every startup makes it.

He hesitated. Would 'you okay?' feel weird to send?

He sent it anyway. "Hey, how's it going?"
A short reply: "It's rough. But still fighting."

When you've celebrated someone genuinely, they pick up when things get hard too.

title: What Changed and What Didn't
description:
The friend he'd seen for the first time in six months — he saw again today.
The plans came together much faster this time.

Last time it took an hour to shake the awkwardness. Today they were talking the moment they sat down.

choices.text: They talked through what had changed and what hadn't
choices.result_text:
"What are you actually into these days?"
That question came naturally.

No shared interests required — the conversation still worked. Maybe that's always what friendship was: someone you can hand the changed parts of yourself to.

He knows now: awkwardness isn't the death of a friendship. Just a gap that needed crossing.

choices.text: Nothing much changed — but the meeting itself was enough
choices.result_text:
"How've you been?" "Fine, you?" "Same."

Not a lot of words. But comfortable ones.

Some relationships are more about form than content, maybe. The fact of meeting saying more than whatever gets said.
